steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Deindividuation: losing your sense of personal identity in a crowd, which can lead to behaviour you would not normally do. Anonymity (e.g. uniforms, masks) reduces self-awareness and increases conformity to group norms.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social Identity Theory (Tajfel & Turner): we derive part of our identity from group membership. Process: social categorisation -> social identification -> social comparison. This can lead to in-group favouritism and out-group discrimination.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Tajfel's minimal group paradigm: even when groups are assigned arbitrarily (e.g. preference for Klee vs Kandinsky), participants favoured their in-group. This shows that even meaningless group distinctions create bias.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Prejudice: a negative attitude towards a group based on stereotypes. Discrimination: unfair treatment based on group membership. Causes: social identity, scapegoating, media representations, and authoritarian personality.

steps.body: Deindividuation = losing personal identity in a crowd. Behaviour follows GROUP NORMS (good or bad). Social Identity Theory: Categorise -> Identify -> Compare. 'Us vs Them' thinking is automatic. Reduce prejudice: contact + superordinate goals + equal status + education.
